MGT 409 · Final project

Donor Diligence Desk

A two-minute, investment-committee style giving memo for any US charity that files a Form 990, written by AI agents that are not allowed to invent a number.

Talha Javed · October 26, 2026
github.com/talha1732/donor-diligence-desk

The problem

Donors want to give well, but checking a charity takes an afternoon

$394B
given by US individuals in 2025; about 18% of a year's giving lands in December
35%
of donors research before giving; 2% compare charities' performance, though 85% say it matters
3 to 6 h
to read three years of IRS Form 990s for three charities by hand (our estimate)

Who: individual donors, giving circles (about 4,000 in the US), small family foundations. None has a program officer. Ratings cover about 15% of charities, and the local ones donors care about are often unrated.

Giving USA 2026; Blackbaud Institute 2026; Money for Good (Hope Consulting, 2010); Charity Navigator; sources in docs/research.md

How it works

Four AI agents between code that handles every number

A fixed pipeline, not a free-roaming boss agent: predictable cost, no loops, every stage testable. gpt-6-luna reads and judges; Python does the arithmetic and the checking.

Demo: one real run

Pick charities, set priorities, watch six agents work

  • Real run: Connecticut Foodshare, Columbus House, IRIS for a New Haven donor
  • Six specialists in parallel read 990 data and websites: 24 tool calls (29 with the auditor's checks)
  • Verifier checked 18 numeric findings: all matched
  • Red-Team Auditor removed 3 claims the evidence did not support
  • 115 seconds, 18 model requests, $0.0085
Live run screen: agent cards, tool calls, spend meter, safety panel
The output

A memo you can check line by line

Action-title headline, summary, recommendation
Every number opens its source and formula
  • 0 to 100 scorecard on five dimensions, re-weight instantly
  • Gaps become questions, drafted as an email
Cost to run

About a cent or less per memo, measured

$0.006
typical 2-charity memo: 56K input tokens (72% cached), 7K output, 45 to 62 seconds
$0.03
per donor per month (5 memos)
$3
per month for 100 donors
$300
per month for 10,000 donors (model only)
  • Code computes every metric, so prompts carry short facts, not raw filings
  • Stable prompts first: 68% of input tokens served from cache, about a third off the bill
  • Caps: 2 searches and 3 pages per charity; $0.10 kill switch per run, $2 per day
  • Tested a lean browsing mode: 6% cheaper, but it cut off a fact near the bottom of a page and cannot reach subpages, so it was not shipped
Safety

Charity websites are untrusted input, and the defenses are tested

0 / 44
instruction-pattern matches reaching the model, defenses on / off (9 attack pages)
0 of 9
live runs with a planted claim in the memo, defenses on (9 of 9 with defenses off)
  • Hidden text removed (white-on-white, display:none, comments, off-screen)
  • Verifier deletes any finding whose numbers do not match the evidence ledger
  • $0.10 per run and $2 per day kill switches; tool and request caps
  • Cross-tested against a second build's 19 attacks: all blocked
  • Sites that cannot be read at all, and missing data, are left out of the score, never counted as 0

What's next

From a working prototype to the December giving season

Limits today

  • Free IRS data lacks program-spending share and runs about a year behind
  • Impact evidence is only what a charity publishes; some sites block automated readers
  • Scores use a documented rubric, a hypothesis rather than a standard

Next month

  • Parse full e-filed 990s for program and fundraising expenses
  • Pilot with a New Haven giving circle in December
  • Send the drafted questions, record answers as evidence, re-score
  • A self-check mode for nonprofit executive directors
